correctness.rationale: In the stated height-at-most-one excursion model the even set of non-flat positions determines the word. For two shared distinct deletion outputs, the Type-A criterion applies to the first-to-last differing interval. The two U/D phases cannot start at the same admissible prefix height; a longer F/U or F/D interval puts UFU or DFD in one phase. The two-letter flat swaps are admissible and realize two distinct deletion outputs, with no validity filter on the outputs. This proves the full graph identification, including absence of interlayer edges. Sliding to the packed set proves connectedness. Toggling the first mixed adjacent pair gives a matching; unmatched even sets occupy whole pairs and no lone last site, and all have position-sum parity t. This certifies the layer and summed optima, including singleton layers and the vacuous two-read condition. Choosing the other positions counts edges per boundary. Moving the rightmost token that needs to move right, or the leftmost needing leftward movement, attains the sorted-coordinate L1 lower bound, proving the distance and diameter formulas. Packed-to-packed paths use only rightward moves; their prerequisites are exactly the rectangular tableau order, so the hook-length count follows. Read RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and distance_check.py; their recorded finite checks are supplementary and were not rerun.
